```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days. A's buyer is an individual paying $10-15/month by self-serve signup, with no procurement, no BAA and no integration. B's own brief documents a long per-practice sales cycle with scope renegotiation.",
    "B's closest precedent, Cydoc, was a nearly identical product built by a clinically credentialed founder over seven years. It reached only four paying customers and $27,900 in 2024 revenue, mostly non-subscription, with $4,000-$6,000 integration cost per practice. That is direct evidence that even a first sale is slow and costly in this niche.",
    "B carries ongoing per-customer setup that a solo operator must clear before any revenue: a HIPAA BAA for each customer, ongoing safeguards, an FDA non-device legal review, and physician liability concerns. A's regulatory need is a one-time privacy policy and terms-of-service consult plus export and delete tooling.",
    "A's channels are cheap and testable: a Product Hunt launch at $200-$2,000 and productivity YouTube sponsorships at $20-$40 CPM. B's main channel is a $3,000-$10,000 conference booth (about $1,850 space-only at smaller shows), and it is the same channel Cydoc used without gaining traction.",
    "A has serious weaknesses: a saturated category with a free incumbent (Obsidian), WorldBrain's failure with the same 'Memex' framing, Tana's pivot away from pure personal knowledge tools, and thin demand quotes. These make A a hard business, but they do not block a first paying customer the way B's sales and compliance barriers do."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The Case For claims that funded competitors charge $99-$500/provider/month 'with apparent traction, proving willingness to pay.' The brief cites only list prices and no customer counts, revenue or usage, so the traction claim is effectively unsourced. B's direct demand evidence is also weak. The Reddit quote is one nurse practitioner's frustration that an employer would not add intake paperwork, which says nothing about a physician paying for an AI note tool. The 8+ hours/week EHR statistic is AMA data relayed second-hand through a competitor's marketing page.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Neither brief shows strong first-party demand: A's demand quotes are a 2020 HN comment and one blog post, and B's are a tangential Reddit post and a competitor-relayed statistic. B has better price-point evidence. A wins mainly because B's best evidence, the Cydoc postmortem, argues directly against a solo operator closing a first sale within 90 days, and A has a low-friction path to one paying user even if it struggles to grow afterward."
}
```
